title: How to Sell Ebooks from Kenya: Everything You Need to Get Your Store Live — No Stripe Required
author: COREMERCH
excerpt: Selling digital products from Nigeria, Ghana, Kenya, Pakistan, Bangladesh, or Zimbabwe is fully operational with sovereign commerce infrastructure that has no geographic restrictions.
imageAlt: Digital creator in Ghana building a sovereign store with crypto payments and NOWPayments
imageCaption: The blockchain has no geographic restrictions — a wallet in Lagos processes identically to one in London.

content.text: Creators in restricted markets are not waiting for Stripe to expand its coverage map. They are not petitioning PayPal to reconsider their country risk model. They are building on [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/full-infrastructure-guide-selling-beats-online-crypto-payments-5|COREMERCH guide to infrastructure]] that was never subject to those decisions in the first place. A static storefront on [[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/cloudflare-workers-[[LINK:https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/crypto-payment-gateways-digital-products-first-principles-definitive-6|Crypto Payment]]-payment-webhooks-what-actually-how-13|cloudflare]] Pages loads in under 200 milliseconds anywhere on earth. NOWPayments accepts payment in USDT, Bitcoin, Solana, and 300 plus other coins from any buyer with a wallet — no account creation, no identity verification, no geography check. The webhook fires the moment the transaction confirms on-chain. The download link arrives in the buyer's inbox within 30 seconds. This is what sovereign commerce infrastructure looks like operating at full capacity from Lagos, Accra, Nairobi, Karachi, Dhaka, or Harare.

This post is part of the COREMERCH infrastructure series. For the complete foundation — every component, every configuration step, and the full deployment sequence — read the pillar guide: Selling Digital Products from Africa: The Complete Infrastructure Guide at https://coremerch.github.io/store/blog/selling-digital-products-africa-step-step-deployment-guide. That guide covers the complete architecture that this post builds on.

content.text: Why This Infrastructure Works When Platforms Fail

The COREMERCH infrastructure is designed to bypass these restrictions, giving you full control over your digital commerce stack. By leveraging GitHub Pages or Cloudflare Pages for hosting, Cloudflare Workers or Google Apps Script for backend logic, and Supabase or Google Sheets for order storage, you can create a sovereign online store that processes payments in cryptocurrencies like USDT on Tron, which settles in under 60 seconds for a fee under $0.10.
What You Need Before You Deploy

Before deploying your digital commerce stack, you need to have a clear understanding of your target audience, the products you want to sell, and the pricing strategy you will use. You also need to set up a digital wallet that supports cryptocurrencies and have a basic understanding of how blockchain-based payments work. Additionally, you need to choose a payment gateway like NOWPayments that supports over 300 cryptocurrencies and has a low fee of 0.5%.
Setting Up Your Payment and Delivery Pipeline

To set up your payment and delivery pipeline, you need to integrate your digital wallet with your payment gateway and configure your online store to accept cryptocurrency payments. You also need to set up a system for delivering your digital products to customers, such as Google Drive or Cloudflare R2. With the Complete Builder Kit, you can get instant access to all the templates and blueprints you need to build and deploy your sovereign digital commerce stack.
Sovereign digital commerce infrastructure gives you full control over your online store.
Going Live and Processing Your First Transaction

Once you have set up your payment and delivery pipeline, you can go live with your online store and start processing transactions. The first transaction is always the most exciting, as it validates your infrastructure and gives you the confidence to scale your business. With Binance P2P supporting naira, cedis, Kenyan shillings, and Pakistani rupees, you can reach a wider audience and increase your sales.
Scaling Once the Infrastructure Is Running

The Edge Commerce Stack that COREMERCH deploys most frequently combines Cloudflare Pages for storefront hosting, Cloudflare Workers for backend webhook handling and order processing, Supabase for order storage, Resend for transactional email delivery, and NOWPayments for crypto payment verification. The total monthly cost is zero. The scale ceiling is significantly higher than what most individual creators need — Cloudflare Workers handles 100,000 requests per day on the free tier, Supabase provides 500MB of PostgreSQL storage, and Resend delivers 3,000 emails per month. For a creator in any country on earth, this stack provides the same infrastructure as a well-funded e-commerce operation at no monthly cost.
How can creators in Africa sell digital products to international buyers?

Creators in Africa can sell digital products to international buyers by using blockchain-based payments and sovereign digital commerce infrastructure. This allows them to bypass platform restrictions and reach a global audience. With the right infrastructure in place, creators can increase their sales and earn a living from their digital products.
Blockchain-based payments allow you to reach a global audience and increase your sales.

If you're looking for a comprehensive solution to build and deploy your sovereign digital commerce stack, consider the Complete Builder Kit, available for $197 at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html. This kit includes all 6 blueprints and 7 templates you need to get started, and it's worth $348 separately.
Your Deployment Checklist

To deploy your sovereign digital commerce stack, follow these steps: set up your digital wallet and choose a payment gateway, integrate your wallet with your payment gateway, configure your online store to accept cryptocurrency payments, set up a system for delivering your digital products, test your infrastructure to ensure it's working correctly, and go live with your online store. You can find more information and resources at https://coremerch.github.io/products.html.
